These numbers are the study's result and may be quoted WITH their label and their limitations: the human arms are MODELLED and not measured, the venue is one Aave-V3-shaped rule tuple, the liquidator is a testnet-shaped LogNormal(median 15 s), and nothing here is a claim about money on BSC mainnet.

design.task: T1 防清算 — liquidation protection. T2 and T3 are not in this study.
design.factors: Shock (4) x Clock (2) x Books (2) = 16 cells, crossed

booksModel.market: One price path shared by every book — they are positions in one market, so the shock is common.
booksModel.liquidator: INDEPENDENT per book, exogenousRng(pathId, 'liquidator', k). Three accounts attract three searchers. This is the choice that favours the sequential human; perfectly correlated liquidators would kill every book at once and hand arm A the axis.
booksModel.agent: Round-robin, one protect per block: book k is broadcast 3 s behind book 0. Conservative — a keeper batching consecutive nonces lands every book in one block, so this over-charges arm A.
booksModel.human: Sequential hands: one notice draw for the portfolio, then +45 s per extra book (REPORT-PLAN §3.1). The human is not given a triage rule; books are worked in index order.

design.armRRemoved: Arm R is removed by the operator's decision and has no substitute. A judge who rejects modelled baselines is left with P.
design.chain: Nothing new on chain. BSC 56 / 97 only. Testnet U and mock tokens are never converted to dollars.

confirmatory.family: REPORT-PLAN §5 pre-registers a Holm-corrected family of four (C1, C1b, C2, C3). T2 and T3 are not in this study, so the family ACTUALLY RUN is two: C1 and C1b. A p corrected over two is not comparable with a p corrected over four, and this record says which was applied.

c1.endpoint: cost-inclusive terminal equity, as a fraction of opening equity, paired

c1b.endpoint: CVaR(5%) of E(T)/E(0) − 1 — the mean of the worst 5% of paths, ranked on each path's own return

ci.method: paired percentile bootstrap over PATHS — both arms recomputed on the same resampled paths

c1b.method: CVaR(5%) is the mean of the worst 5% of paths, ranked on E(T)/E(0) − 1 — a SCALE-FREE endpoint, so the tail is not a selection on portfolio size. The gap is CVaR(A) - CVaR(H2), already a fraction of opening equity; the interval and the p-value come from resampling PATHS with replacement and recomputing both arms on the same resample, so the pairing is preserved inside every replicate.
c1b.reportedQuantity: gap in CVaR(5%) of E(T)/E(0) − 1, arm A minus arm H2, in bps of opening equity. The −1 shifts both arms' levels by the same constant, so the GAP is identical on E(T)/E(0) and on the return; the LEVELS are not, which is why they are labelled separately.

holm.comparison: A-vs-H2 · gap in CVaR(5%) of E(T)/E(0) − 1

confirmatory.note: Both tests are TWO-SIDED, which is the conservative choice against a pre-registered direction: a one-sided test at the same alpha would halve each p. The observed direction is recorded separately so a result in the unexpected direction would be visible rather than absorbed.

booksInteraction.question: Does the agent's advantage GROW with the number of books? Sequential hands cost 45 s per extra book; a round-robin keeper costs one block. The difference of differences is the answer.
booksInteraction.caveat: Books is a crossed factor with 8 cells per level, so this is a within-design contrast rather than a separate experiment; it is still EXPLORATORY — REPORT-PLAN §5 confirms C1 alone on this task, and no correction is applied to it. The equity MEDIANS on this axis are dominated by exact ties (arm A and arm H1 both survive every grind and crash path, so half the matrix contributes zeros); the book-survival rows and the material medians are the statistics that carry the effect.

mixture.question: MVP Finding 10: the pooled median names a cluster boundary rather than a typical path, and the fraction of paths on which protection BINDS is a headline quantity in its own right.
mixture.reading: The honest sentence is 'on the paths where protection binds, the median gap is X, and that is Y% of paths', not 'the agent is worth the pooled median'.

survivalUncertainty.question: For every survival proportion the report draws or prints, and every difference between two of them a sentence asserts, how much of it is resolvable at this sample size?
survivalUncertainty.metric: book-level survival — the fraction of POSITIONS kept, books survived over books held
survivalUncertainty.whyBookLevel: A portfolio survives only when every book does, so portfolio survival is a 3-of-3 event at three books and a 1-of-1 at one: arm A's is 86.5% at 1 book and 56.8% at 3, while its BOOK survival over the same two levels moves only 86.5% to 76.8%. The difference between those two falls is the Books axis and not anything an arm did. Book survival divides the axis out of numerator and denominator together, which is why §4 calls it the only survival figure comparable across the design. Portfolio survival is published beside it per arm and per book level; it is never pooled into a figure.
survivalUncertainty.rateMethod: Wilson score interval at 95%, twice. Once over the raw book count, and once over the effective sample size n / DEFF, where DEFF = 1 + (mean cluster size - 1) * rho and rho is Donner's ANOVA intra-cluster correlation over PATHS — because a three-book portfolio's three books are replayed against one price path and are not three independent draws. Wilson rather than Wald because several of these rates sit at or beside 0 and 1, where Wald either leaves [0, 1] or collapses to a point of zero width.
survivalUncertainty.contrastMethod: Cluster percentile bootstrap over whole paths, 10,000 resamples. A path carries both arms' outcomes and all of its books, so resampling paths keeps the pairing the design paid for and the clustering the book count creates. Contrasts between two disjoint path sets — the two clocks, the two book levels — resample each set independently and difference inside the loop.
survivalUncertainty.standing: EXPLORATORY AND UNCORRECTED. No Holm, no multiplicity adjustment of any kind, over 185 rates and 55 contrasts. A handful would exclude zero at 95% by arithmetic alone. Read the large ones; do not count the significant ones.
survivalUncertainty.monteCarlo: Every interval here is Monte Carlo sampling uncertainty — how far a re-run with fresh seeds would be expected to move the number. None of it is a confidence statement about real positions on BNB Chain, and nothing on this axis is a measurement of a human.
survivalUncertainty.scaleDeclaration: The rate itself is `armSummary.bookSurvivalRate` in booksScale.declarations — scale-free, because the denominator grows with the axis exactly as the numerator does. An interval around a declared quantity, in that quantity's own unit, inherits its declaration, exactly as C1's bootstrapCi sits inside the declaration on C1's median. Rows marked within-level hold one book level and the builder throws if one does not; the two between-level contrasts are a deliberate comparison ACROSS the axis, which is the sanctioned way to talk about it rather than a pooling of it.

wick1blockLoss.preRegistered: Arm A was pre-registered to LOSE on wick-1block against passive, by roughly one protect's keeper fee plus one transaction's gas, because the market recovers and the position would have repaired itself. corrections.provenance: An independent replay of all 8,000 book-level ledgers in a second language recomputed every headline in this study from the stored event records. Every one of them matched, C1 included. What it found instead were three defects in the analysis layer: an estimator, a renderer and a label. A later independent verifier, reading the corrected document, found two more — both in section 9, both the same class as the first, and both missed by the sweep that had been run over the first three because that sweep enumerated by SECTION and by NUMERAIRE while these two are in seconds and in counts. Five defects; four of them one class — every one except the dropped-disclosure renderer — and four separate passes to find those four. That is the reason this report now carries a mechanism rather than another patch.

booksScale.question: Not 'which section is this in' and not 'is it denominated in N' — four passes enumerated that way and each found one more. The only question that closes the class: DOES RESTRICTING THE POPULATION TO ONE BOOK LEVEL MOVE THIS NUMBER, AND IF SO, HOW?
booksScale.method: Every summary object the report prints is rebuilt three times — over the pooled population, over the one-book records alone, and over the three-book records alone — and every numeric leaf of the three is compared by path. A leaf whose levels agree is scale-free and needs nothing. A leaf whose pooled value equals one level's value is that level's statistic under a pooled label. A leaf whose levels sit on the books ratio is denominated in the axis. A leaf whose pooled value is near neither level names no record. The last three require a declaration in BOOKS_SCALE_DECLARATIONS, a scale-free declaration is refused on all three, and an undeclared one fails the run rather than printing.

chokepoint.quantity: median E(T)/E(0) - 1, arm A
chokepoint.unit: fraction of opening equity · per arm-path

declaration.why: Each run's outcome is divided by THAT run's own opening equity before the median is taken, so a one-book and a three-book path enter on one scale.

chokepoint.quantity: CVaR(5%) of E(T)/E(0) - 1, arm A
chokepoint.unit: fraction of opening equity · per arm-path

declaration.why: The tail is SELECTED on the return, not on numeraire, so a three-book path can enter it. Selecting it in N is defect 1 and this declaration is what refuses it.

chokepoint.quantity: mean transactions per run, arm A
chokepoint.unit: transactions · per arm-path

declaration.why: Same quantity as the protect count on every arm here, and it is what the gas line is multiplied by.
declaration.readerWarning: Support 0..1 at one book and 0..3 at three. The pooled mean describes neither level; the per-level means are printed beside it.

chokepoint.quantity: mean protects per run, arm A
chokepoint.unit: protects · per arm-path

declaration.why: It is the keeper's whole workload per run, and the gas bound is charged against it, so the pooled figure is the one the cost table needs.
declaration.readerWarning: The support is 0..1 protects on a one-book run and 0..3 on a three-book one, so this pooled mean is set by how many cells hold three books as much as by how the arm behaves. §9 prints it per book level beside this.

chokepoint.quantity: median latency to the last book protected, arm A
chokepoint.unit: seconds · per arm-path

declaration.why: The single 'how fast is this arm' number the secondaries table is read for.
declaration.readerWarning: At one book this is the time to protect the only book; at three it is the time to protect the LAST of three under the round-robin, which is a different quantity as well as a larger one. Both are printed per level.

blindSpots: IT SWEEPS THE BUILDERS IT IS GIVEN, and that is the largest hole left. Adding a STATISTIC to a summary the census already probes is caught automatically — the leaf appears and must be declared. Adding a whole new SUMMARY FUNCTION and printing it, without adding it to the probe list in `booksScaleAudit`, is not caught by anything. Forgetting a statistic is now impossible; forgetting a builder is merely harder.
It sweeps the statistics the scoring layer COMPUTES. A number a renderer forms itself — a difference of two printed values, a percentage taken in a template — is not a leaf and is not swept.
It compares the two levels this study ran. A quantity that is scale-free at 1 and 3 books and not at 10 would pass, and there is no 10-book level to catch it.

It reads magnitudes, not meanings. Two levels can agree numerically while the quantity means different things on each — arm A's latency at three books is the time to the LAST book, and only the unit-of-analysis field says so.

A leaf classified level-varying is reported and not blocked. That is deliberate — the Books axis is a real effect and its statistics are supposed to move — but it is the class a genuinely new defect would most easily hide in.
It cannot see a defect in a number the report prints from a constant rather than from the records.

seeds.rngScheme: mulberry32 seeded by xmur3 over (schema, kind, ...parts). Exogenous streams exogenousRng(pathId, 'price') and exogenousRng(pathId, 'liquidator', book) exclude the ARM, so every arm faces the same market and the same three liquidators — that is the pairing. Arm streams armRng(pathId, arm, stream) include the arm and are keyed by NAME, so adding H1 and H3 perturbed no draw of A, H2 or P. Book 0's liquidator seed is the pre-Books seed unchanged.

parameterContext.note: A repayment retires debt rather than destroying it, so one protect costs the keeper fee plus gas and nothing else. Almost the whole A-vs-H2 effect is therefore AVOIDED SEIZURE, and what a seizure is worth is NOT the liquidationPenalty memo (c_s*P_s - d_c) but its cost to terminal equity (c_s*P(T) - d_c). Both are in mechanism.avoidedSeizureCost. The effect is SUPER-LINEAR in the bonus wherever the price keeps falling after the seizure; mechanism.bonusSensitivity rescores it rather than reasoning about it.
